title: CRLR/411/2022 of RAKESH KUMAR PAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 411 of 2022
Rakesh Kumar Pal ...Revisionist
Versus

State of Uttarakhandand Another ...Respondents
Present:-
Mr. P.C. Petshali for the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the
following:-
 (1) Judgment and order dated 30.09.2021,
passed in Misc. Criminal Case No. 156 of
2016, Smt. Anshu Singh Versus Rakesh
Kumar Pal, by the court of Judicial
Magistrate, Kashipur, District Udham Singh
Nagar ("the case"). By it, an application
under Section 12 of the Protection of Women
from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 ("the Act")
has been allowed and various directions
have been issued to the revisionist including
payment of Rs. 3,000/- per month to the
respondent no.2. and also directed the
revisionist to make available accommodation

2
to the respondent no.2 or else to pay her Rs.
1,000/- per month as house rent allowance.
And;
 (2) Judgment and order dated 13.06.2022,
passed in Criminal Appeal No.219 of 2021,
Rakesh Kumar Pal Vs. Smt. Anshu Singh, by
the court of 1st Additional Sessions Judge,
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar by
which the impugned judgment and order
dated 30.09.2021, passed in the case has
been upheld.
2. Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and
perused the record.
3. In the revision, the main ground taken is that the
respondent no.2 is not in the domestic relationship with the
revisionist. It is the case that in order to construe domestic
relationship, the parties should live together in a shared
household.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist would submit
that the private respondent never stayed with the revisionist
in his shared household. Therefore, she does not fall within
the definition of domestic relationship and is not entitled to
get any relief under the provisions of the Act. Apart from it,
the rent of the residence has been challenged on the ground

3
that parties have secured divorce. Therefore, now there is no
question of the private respondent staying with the
revisionist in his shared household. It is also argued that in
such eventuality, the revisionist should not be asked to pay
any house rent allowance.
5. The revisionist and the respondent no.2 were
married on 27.05.2015. After marriage, it is the case of the
respondent no.2 that the revisionist took her in a hotel.
There he committed cruelty on her, which resulted into
return of the respondent no.2 in her father's house next
morning. Thereafter, the dispute further flared up and the
parties did not stay together.
6. Domestic Relationship has been defined under
Section 2(f) of the Act. A similar issue was argued before the
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prabha Tyagi Vs.
Kamlesh Devi (2022) 8 SCC 90. The Hon'ble Supreme Court
observed that it is not necessary that the parties should stay
together in a shared household so as to construe the
domestic relationship. In Para 43 to 45, the Hon'ble
Supreme Court observed as hereunder:-
 "43. If a woman in a domestic relationship seeks
to enforce her right to reside in a shared household,
irrespective of whether she has resided therein at all or
not, then the said right can be enforced under sub-section (1) of Section 17 of the DV Act. If her right to
reside in a shared household is resisted or restrained
by the respondent(s) then she becomes an aggrieved

4
person and she cannot be evicted, if she has already
been living in the shared household or excluded from
the same or any part of it if she is not actually residing
therein. In other words, the expression "right to reside
in the shared household" is not restricted to only
actual residence, as, irrespective of actual residence, a
woman in a domestic relationship can enforce her right
to reside in the shared household.
44. Thus, a woman cannot be excluded from the
shared household even if she has not actually resided
therein that is why the expression "shall not be evicted
or excluded from the shared household" has been
intentionally used in sub-section (2) of Section 17. This
means if a woman in a domestic relationship is an
aggrieved person and she is actually residing in the
shared household, she cannot be evicted except in
accordance with the procedure established by law.
Similarly, a woman in a domestic relationship who is
an aggrieved person cannot be excluded from her right
to reside in the shared household except in accordance
with the procedure established by law.
45. Therefore, the expression "right to reside in the
shared household" would include not only actual
residence but also constructive residence in the shared
household i.e. right to reside therein which cannot be
excluded vis-à-vis an aggrieved person except in
accordance with the procedure established by law. If a
woman is sought to be evicted or excluded from the
shared household she would be an aggrieved person in
which event sub-section (2) of Section 17 would apply."
7. It is the right of a woman to stay in the shared
household, which may not be excluded. Staying together in
the shared household is not the defining criteria. Therefore,
the arguments that since the respondent no.2 never resided
with the revisionist, she does not fall within the definition
relationship, does not merit for acceptance. Insofar as home
rent allowance is concerned, it is not the case that there was
no domestic relationship.

5
8. Having considered, this Court is of the view that
the impugned judgments and orders do not warrant any
interference. They are in accordance with law. Accordingly,
the revision deserves to be dismissed at the stage of
admission itself.
9. The revision is dismissed in liminie.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 28.09.2022
Ravi Bisht
